panels.description: Wide, full page width. A road clinging to the edge of the land. On the left, palm groves and pepper gardens climb gentle slopes; on the right, low cliffs drop to a strip of sand and a flat grey ocean. Two small riders seen from behind, heading south in a salt haze.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: They did not take me to a palace.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The bulls were gone. This time I rode, though not as I had once ridden.

panels.description: Medium, the two riders side by side, riding toward us. Nagoji on a small, rough-coated coastal horse with a suspicious eye, smaller than any Deccan mare. Nagoji is bare-headed and unarmed: simple cream shirt, cotton dhoti, long curly hair tied back, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud; no sword, no sash, no turban. His bandaged hands are light on the reins and his spine is straight. Ibrahim on a sturdy pony on the near side, his LEFT cheek turned to us so the scar from his LEFT ear to the jaw reads: shorter than the fishermen but broader, white turban, short grey-flecked beard, dark short coat with bulging pockets over a pale vest and white mundu. He pats one pocket. He has caught Nagoji looking.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Gifts. Information costs, *bhau*. So do favours.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: When we reach the hall, remember that.

panels.description: The largest panel on the page. The road dips to a narrow inlet, dark and still. Boats drawn up along its banks, broad-bellied cargo craft and slender river canoes, cooking smoke drifting. On the rise beyond, an outer wall of rough red stone blocks topped with a musketeers' parapet; inside it a long hall on wooden pillars carved with vines and tigers, its long side open toward the sea. Behind, on higher ground, a rampart runs inland along the shape of the land. Not large. Purpose in every line.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM (small, soft)
copy.text: This is only one claw. The kingdom itself is the beast.

panels.description: The gate. Travancore guards in white cotton with dark sashes, matchlocks and spears, alert but not nervous. One raises a hand in greeting to Ibrahim (white turban, short grey-flecked beard, dark short coat with bulging pockets, scar from his LEFT ear to the jaw). Nagoji in the foreground, bare-headed and unarmed in his cream shirt, turning his head sharply at the words.

copy.speaker: GUARD
copy.text: The king is in council. You are expected.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In most kingdoms I had known, a stranger waited days for an audience. Here the king himself waited at the end of the road.

panels.description: Narrow strip, bottom. Nagoji dismounted, bare-headed and unarmed in his cream shirt, his bandaged hand on the coastal horse's neck. The horse has tossed its head away from him, toward the groom taking its reins. Nagoji is still patting a neck that is already leaving.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Kanka would have nudged my shoulder.

panels.description: From the top of a short flight of stone steps, behind Nagoji and Ibrahim (white turban, dark short coat) as they step out of the glare into a cooler hall. High roof, dark rafters, mats on the floor. Men sit cross-legged in loose rows, leaving a clear lane down the centre to a raised platform at the far end. The long side of the hall on screen LEFT stands open between pillars, and through it, below, the sea.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In the Deccan, kings received men in high halls thick with incense, with carpets to muffle footsteps and paintings to remind visitors who held power.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Here, when the hall fell quiet, you could still hear the sea.

panels.description: Large. Down the clear lane to the far end: a slightly raised wooden platform, and on it MARTHANDA VARMA (attach `concepts/varma-v1.png` and use the sheet for his FACE ONLY). Tall, bare-chested, a single cream-and-gold cloth thrown over one shoulder, gold necklaces, simple Vaishnavite lines on his forehead. A cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest, no crown. A spear rests against his shoulder. A rolled map lies open on the mat before him; a sword lies within easy reach, its hilt worn smooth by use rather than polished for show. He is looking at the map, not toward the camera. At his left hand (screen right), small and in shadow, Ramayyan sits at a low table in plain white cloth. The open side of the hall runs down screen left, and sea light falls across the platform from that side.

Close. Ibrahim at Nagoji's ear, lips barely moving, hand resting on a clinking pocket (white turban, short grey-flecked beard, dark short coat, scar from his LEFT ear to the jaw). Nagoji in profile, listening: bare-headed, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin. Beyond them, small and soft at the far end of the lane, Marthanda Varma on his platform, in his cream-and-gold turban with its jewelled peacock-feather crest. The open side of the hall on screen left.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Marthanda Varma. And his diwan.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Remember what I said about gifts.

panels.description: Medium, beside the platform: RAMAYYAN. Thin frame, sharp fine features, receding hair; his upper body wrapped in plain white cloth (not bare-chested), no jewellery, no crest, no spear. A low table before him with palm-leaf bundles, an ink pot and a stylus. His eyes are on the newcomers, and on everything else. The king is out of frame. In the near foreground, two seated men lean their heads together, whispering. Sea light from the open side falls from screen left.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Ramayyan. He spoke Persian and Dutch and every trade tongue of this coast.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. From the entrance end, low behind the shoulders of the seated rows: Nagoji walking into the clear space, small against the length of the hall, heads along both rows turning to follow him. Ibrahim (white turban, dark short coat) a step behind him at the start of the lane. Marthanda Varma small on his platform at the far end, in his cream-and-gold turban with its jewelled peacock-feather crest. The open side of the hall on screen left.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The back of my neck prickled, as it always did when I walked alone into a space where everyone else already knew their place.

panels.description: From the entrance end, the open side of the hall on screen left. Nagoji bowing, bare-headed and unarmed in his cream shirt and dhoti, bandaged hands: not as deeply as a subject would, but enough to set the man on the platform apart from a fellow soldier. Ibrahim a pace behind him and to one side, toward the open side (white turban, short grey-flecked beard, dark short coat), smooth, one open hand gesturing forward toward Nagoji. Marthanda Varma small on his platform at the far end, eyes still on his map (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest), Ramayyan in white cloth at his left hand (screen right).

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Your Majesty. This is the Maratha rider I wrote of.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: He comes from Portuguese chains and storm water, and he carries knowledge of both.

panels.description: Tight horizontal strip across Varma's eyes as they leave the map and settle on Nagoji. Dark. Steady. Nothing soft, nothing careless. Only Varma's eyes and brow in frame, face from the sheet only; if any headwear shows at the top edge it is the cream-and-gold turban. No other figure.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The kind of eyes that measure before they strike.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had seen them in generals' tents, and in men who held small forts against impossible odds.

panels.description: Two-shot from behind Nagoji's shoulder (bare-headed, curly hair tied back, cream shirt), the open side of the hall on screen left. Varma on the platform speaks, looking only at Nagoji (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest; bare chest, cream-and-gold cloth over one shoulder, gold necklaces). Ramayyan at the king's left hand (screen right), thin, in plain white cloth, no jewellery, translates a heartbeat later without taking his eyes off Nagoji either.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: [in Malayalam]

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: The Maharaja asks if you were on the ship that broke near our fishermen's village.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Yes. I was.

panels.description: Wide and flat, the rhythm panel: a side view across the hall, with the open sea side behind the camera and the closed wall behind the figures. Left to right: Marthanda Varma on his raised platform (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest; bare chest, cream-and-gold cloth), Ramayyan at his low table at the platform's front corner (thin, plain white cloth wrapped over his upper body, no jewellery), and Nagoji standing on the floor below (village shirt and dhoti, bandaged hands, bare-headed, no chains, no weapon). Stagger the balloons left to right in the order Ramayyan, Nagoji, Ramayyan, Nagoji so the questions come fast.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: He asks if you rode for the Peshwa.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I did.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: You raided Portuguese outposts on the western roads that feed their ports.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I did.

panels.description: Varma's hand in the foreground, two fingers extended toward Nagoji's bandaged fingers: only his hand, a gold bangle and the edge of his cream-and-gold cloth are in frame, his head out of frame. Nagoji's wrapped hands at the far edge of frame, still at his sides against his cream shirt.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: They questioned you.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: They tried.

panels.description: Small. Varma, close, facing the camera, the open side of the hall behind him on screen left (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest; gold necklaces). Something like amusement at the corners of his eyes, already fading. His eyes have moved on before any translation could have reached him. No other figure in frame.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: If he understood my answers without his minister's help, he gave no sign beyond the speed of his eyes.

panels.description: Reverse angle from the platform, the open side of the hall on screen right. Ramayyan in the near foreground at screen left (thin, plain white cloth, no jewellery), pointing with his stylus to a mat laid a few paces from the platform. Nagoji, bare-headed in his cream shirt, lowering himself onto it, stiff, favouring healing wounds.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Sit. Speak. Tell him how they fight now on your coast.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: How their forts stand, how their captains think, how quickly they bring ships when a local chief resists.

panels.description: Reverse angle from the platform, the open side of the hall on screen right. Nagoji seated on the mat, talking, one bandaged hand shaping a low wall in the air. Bleeding in behind him like a stain rather than a clean flashback border (the Chapter 1, panel 6.5 device): a Portuguese bastion at Chaul, thick and low, a cannonball skipping off its slope in a spray of stone dust.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For the next while, time lost its edges.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: At Chaul and Daman they build bastions thick and low, so cannonballs skip off instead of biting deep.

panels.description: Large, the page's biggest panel. The stain shifts and softens, because this is hearsay, not memory. It holds only two things: an anonymous padre, a stranger we have never met, in a plain black cassock with no white collar tab, walking ahead with a cross held high; and behind him a column of Portuguese musketeers in broad tilted hats and buff leather coats with matchlocks, not red, not blue. Nagoji small at the lower edge, seated on his mat, still talking. At the foreground edge, Varma's hand makes one small tap on the spear shaft; only the hand and the shaft are in frame.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Our clerks said their padres walk ahead of the soldiers talking of one God, while the men behind count how many guns a king can spare.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: We heard of rajas who signed, thinking European friends would keep neighbours away. They had invited a hungry wolf into their courtyards.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Varma leaning forward over the unrolled map (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest; bare chest, gold necklaces), one finger on a point where a river mouth meets the sea. Inset, top left corner of the panel: Ramayyan's hand and stylus, still until now, scratching fast on a palm leaf.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI (off, in the inset)
copy.text: And their infantry do not know what to do with sudden horse on the flank.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: [in Malayalam]

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Here. This river mouth. How many days from their nearest stronghold at full sail?

panels.description: Reverse angle from the platform, the open side of the hall on screen right. Nagoji on his mat, bare-headed, eyes closed. Behind him, the stain: the coastline seen from a galloping horse's back, sails far out on the water, a Portuguese warehouse burning on a quay at night.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I thought of wind, and of how many days their replacement ships had taken to arrive.

panels.description: Nagoji opening his eyes, answering the king directly. Reverse angle, the open side on screen right.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If the wind favours them, three days. Four if they are unlucky.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Longer if someone whispers wrong directions into the ear of a pilot.

panels.description: Two-shot, platform, the open side of the hall on screen left. Varma's head lifted from the map, eyes narrowed, mouth open on a sharp word (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest). At his left hand (screen right) Ramayyan, thin, in plain white cloth, lips still closed, stylus paused mid-stroke: the king has reacted before the translation.

copy.speaker: VARMA (sharp)
copy.text: [in Malayalam]

panels.description: Nagoji, level, speaking to the king and not to the diwan. Reverse angle, the open side on screen right.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: You mistrust pilots?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I mistrust everyone who touches a coin.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: But men who steer ships can be made to see profit in many directions.

panels.description: Two-shot, platform, the open side of the hall on screen left. The corner of Varma's mouth twitches; he does not turn his head (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest). At his left hand (screen right) Ramayyan, in plain white cloth, is already writing, and does not look up either.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Ram.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (soft)
copy.text: Already marked, Maharaja.

panels.description: Wide, from the entrance end, the open side of the hall on screen left. The hall gone still, as if waiting for something. Marthanda Varma on his platform speaks at length, even-toned, the spear upright beside him (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest). Ramayyan in white cloth at his left hand. Nagoji seated on his mat before the platform, his back to us. The seated rows motionless. Through the open side, the sea.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: [in Malayalam]

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I caught none of the words. Only the weight.

panels.description: Low angle from floor level just before the platform, looking up past its edge, the open side of the hall on screen left. Ramayyan at near right (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth wrapped over his upper body, no jewellery), translating, his stylus held still above the leaf. Behind him and to the left, Marthanda Varma sits motionless with his spear upright (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest).

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: He says you speak as if you have counted men and ships for years.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Yet your own masters failed to keep you from their dungeons.

panels.description: Reverse angle from the platform, the open side of the hall on screen right. Nagoji on his mat, bare-headed in his cream shirt. Jaw set; he does not drop his eyes. His bandaged hands have closed on his knees, gripping the cloth.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was not meant as an insult. It was simple fact. Still, it stung.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Any war has its losses. I misjudged a patrol near the coast. I paid the price.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: That does not make my other calculations less true.

panels.description: Wide from behind Nagoji's mat, the open side of the hall on screen left. On the platform Marthanda Varma, unreadable, speaks briefly (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest). At his left hand (screen right) Ramayyan, in white cloth, turns his head across the hall toward Ibrahim, who stands at the open-side edge of the clear space (screen left) with his hands folded over his pockets (white turban, short grey-flecked beard, dark short coat).

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: [in Malayalam]

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: He says, perhaps.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: And he asks Ibrahim if he trusts you.

panels.description: Medium, seen from the platform side, the open side of the hall on screen right. Ibrahim at the open-side edge of the clear space, easy, spreading his hands: white turban, short grey-flecked beard, dark short coat with bulging pockets over a pale vest and white mundu. He faces the platform, so the open side is at his left, and the sea light from it catches the scar along his LEFT jaw. Pillars and bright sea behind him.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: As far as one can trust a man who owes you his life and hates the same enemies.

copy.speaker: IBRAHIM
copy.text: Beyond that, trust is for priests.

panels.description: Small panel, one moment only. Varma with his head tipped back a fraction in a single short laugh (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest). No other figure.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A dry sound that needed no translation.

panels.description: The page's largest panel, wide, from the hall, the open side on screen left. Varma, after a long silent look at the man on the mat, sweeps one hand toward the open side, where the inlet, the moored boats and the red stone outer wall show below (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest; bare chest, cream-and-gold cloth, gold necklaces). Ramayyan at his left hand (screen right), thin, in plain white cloth, translating.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: [in Malayalam]

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: He says they already have horse from the Nayak of Madurai, and Nair warriors who fight on foot or on small horses in this soil.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: They have Dutch fortifications in their minds, thanks to other Europeans who chose to be practical rather than loyal.

panels.description: Close on Varma, face unreadable, eyes on the guest below him; the question is his (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest; gold necklaces). The open side of the hall behind him on screen left. The diwan is off panel. No other figure in frame.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN (off)
copy.text: He asks what you add that he does not already have.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was the same question they had asked in the compound. But this man could, with a word, send me back to the Portuguese.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Point-of-view shot from a seated position on the mat before the platform, looking sideways out between the pillars of the open side of the hall, no figures in the foreground: the inlet below, the moored boats, men small as ants along the shore unloading sacks and checking nets. Beyond them the sea, flat and deceptive, to a hard, empty horizon. Keep the sky open for two captions.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Somewhere beyond that horizon sat Goa, with its dungeons.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Somewhere farther still, Dutch hulls cut through foaming water, carrying men who believed pepper and souls could belong to them by right.

panels.description: Reverse angle from the platform, the open side of the hall on screen right. Nagoji on his mat, bare-headed, bandaged hands on his knees, his eyes coming back from the open side to the king. Slow. He is not pleading; he is laying out terms.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You have horse from Madurai. You have Nair warriors who know this land as they know their own pulse.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You have guns and forts and men from across the sea who teach you how Europeans think.

panels.description: Large, full width, the page's biggest panel, about 40 percent of the page. The stain again, the largest yet, in warm stained tones: Kanka, the black mare of Chapter 1, on wet sand near Chaul, and low over her neck the memory rider, Nagoji BEFORE his capture, in Maratha cavalry dress (rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, talwar), hands unbandaged. Other Maratha riders in turbans and cream tunics come in beside him. A line of Portuguese musketeers (broad tilted hats, buff leather coats, matchlocks; not British red, not Dutch blue) flinching and falling out of order as the horses come in at an angle they never drilled for. No blood. At the bottom edge, in normal colour, the present-day Nagoji small, seated on his mat: bare-headed, cream shirt, bandaged hands, speaking.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: What you do not yet have is someone who has ridden into a European line and felt it break.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Someone who has watched their neat formations falter not from fear of God, but because a hoof struck at the right moment in the right place.

panels.description: Narrow, cold. The stain turns: only Keshavrao's eyes, huge in storm light, rain across them, at the hatch of the breaking ship. He is about nineteen, beardless, with no scar, black hair hacked short and plastered wet. No other figure.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Keshavrao.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: And the weight I now carried.

panels.description: Medium side view across the hall, as in 4.1, with the open sea side behind the camera. Nagoji on his mat at screen right, leaning in toward the platform edge at screen left, voice lower and harder: bare-headed, cream shirt, bandaged hands. Dark rafters and open hall space above him for the balloons.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I can help you turn speed into a weapon against men who think their guns make them untouchable.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I can show your riders where to strike, when to pull away, how to make men who drilled on flat European fields die confused on this coast.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. From the hall, the open side on screen left: the hall silent, a bird on the parapet outside, waves on the sand below. Varma on his platform taps the butt of his spear against the mat, once, twice (two small motion ticks), eyes never leaving the man on the mat (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest).

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Ram.

panels.description: Medium on Ramayyan at his low table (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth wrapped over his upper body, no jewellery), having inclined his head to the king, now turned to the man on the mat below and speaking to him directly, in Konkani, before any word from the king. The king is out of frame. Sea light from screen left.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: The Madurai horsemen know the straight charge. They do not know the feint and vanish the way Deccan riders do.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Our Maravar riders fight bravely, but not yet with discipline against guns.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: You could help shape that.

panels.description: Two-shot, platform, the open side of the hall on screen left. Varma with a thin smile for his minister, his gaze already back on the mat below as he speaks briefly (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest). At his left hand (screen right) Ramayyan, in white cloth, amused. Nagoji is out of frame.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: [in Malayalam]

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: He says I always see the two faces of the coin. And he says, very well, Nagoji Sawant.

panels.description: Tight on Ramayyan, still faintly amused, eyes sharp on the man below, delivering it lightly (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth, no jewellery).

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: For now, you are not a guest. You are not yet a servant either.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: You are an experiment.

panels.description: Full width. Varma in profile in the near left third, facing screen right, glancing out toward the open side of the hall (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest). The view between the pillars fills the right two thirds: below the fort, a narrow strip of wet sand pinned between a low laterite bluff crowned with coconut palms and the sea. This is the ground of Chapter 7; plant it clearly. Nagoji is out of frame.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: [in Malayalam]

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Outside this fort a strip of shore runs along the sea, too wet for most cavalry, too narrow for big batteries. It is where the Dutch will expect us to be weakest.

panels.description: Full width, bottom. From the entrance end, high, the open side of the hall on screen left. Nagoji small on his mat before the platform, bare-headed in his cream shirt; Marthanda Varma (a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest) and Ramayyan (plain white cloth, at the king's left hand) on the platform above him.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Take the Madurai horse and a hundred Maravar riders, and show him something there he has not already imagined.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: If you are wrong, you will find Travancore worse than the Portuguese.

panels.description: Reverse angle from the platform, the open side of the hall on screen right. Nagoji on his feet before the platform, straightening despite the pull of healing wounds: bare-headed, cream shirt, dhoti, bandaged hands, unarmed.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: As he commands.

panels.description: Two-shot, platform, the open side of the hall on screen left. Varma, voice lower, looking only at the man below (face from the sheet only; a cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest). At his left hand Ramayyan, in white cloth, translating quietly. Nagoji is out of frame.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: [in Malayalam]

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: He says I am to give you what you need. And you are not to waste men.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: He has spent too many lives to sit on that mat. He does not throw them away lightly, not even when the gods demand it.

panels.description: Outside. Ramayyan (thin, plain white cloth, no jewellery), palm leaves under one arm, leads Nagoji out between the carved pillars onto the top of the stone steps. Nagoji is bare-headed and unarmed in his cream shirt. Wind off the sea in his hair, the surf loud below.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Come. Let us see what a storm can do when given horse instead of chains.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Storms had tried to kill me. Now I would learn whether I could become one.

panels.description: Medium close on Nagoji's hip and hand: his bandaged hand has gone to his hip and rests on the plain knot of his cotton dhoti, below the hem of his cream shirt. The hip is bare of any weapon: NO sword, NO scabbard, NO sash, NO belt. The stone step and the bright sea beyond are out of focus.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (italic)
copy.text: *I will serve this king. I will harden his riders and break his enemies.*

copy.speaker: CAPTION (italic)
copy.text: *When that debt is paid, I will turn north again, find Chimaji, and burn the Portuguese out of Goa, stone by bloody stone.*

panels.description: Full width, bottom. Nagoji from behind at the top of the steps, bare-headed, cream shirt and dhoti, his bandaged hand still resting at his hip on the dhoti knot: NO sword, NO scabbard, NO sash. Ramayyan small at lower left, already going down the steps toward the shore. Below and beyond, the coast and the sea. Nagoji's head is turned to screen right, looking up the coastline.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (separate, weighted)
copy.text: For now, Travancore was the forge. But the blade was meant for another war.

frames.review_note: Acceptable. Minor points: Nagoji's hair is drawn as a half-up knot on the crown with the curls loose below. The bible allows 'tied back', but neighbouring panels show it loose, and chapter 17 makes his first hair knot a story beat. His lost-profile jaw has a faint dark shadow that could read as stubble, though it is only a few pixels at this scale. His horse is mid-chestnut rather than dark liver-chestnut. A tiny lighthouse-like tower stands on the far hazy headland. Geography is correct: heading south on the Malabar coast with the sea on the right. The coats match the pre-generation note (flaxen-maned chestnut for Nagoji, black-maned dark brown pony for Ibrahim). Wrists are bandaged. No text. The upper right half is wide clear sky for both captions. The faces listed are the riders' heads, seen from behind.

v02 is clean and follows the correction. The background is now the Travancore coastal road: palms with pepper vines, laterite cliffs, sand and a hazy sea. There are no European buildings. Nagoji is on screen left on the small chestnut with the flaxen mane. Ibrahim is on screen right on the dark brown pony with the black mane, patting a bulging vest pocket and looking at Nagoji. His scar is on the correct (left) cheek, on the screen-right side of his face. Minor points: (1) Ibrahim's scar is a pinkish line, not fully pale, but it matches his sheet's detail. (2) Nagoji's sleeves are rolled to mid-forearm instead of reaching the bandaged wrists. The bandages cover his wrists and fingers are bare, which is acceptable. (3) Note only: Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging drop, not a stud. The open sky across the upper centre and right gives room for both Ibrahim balloons. v01 is rejected because it shows a European church and fort in the background.

v02 is acceptable and follows the correction. It is drawn in the inked line-and-wash style. It shows the still inlet with cargo boats and canoes, cooking smoke at right, the rough red laterite outer wall with a loopholed parapet, and the long tiled hall on dark pillars carved with coiling vines and tigers. The rampart runs up the higher ground behind with a Kerala-roofed watchtower. Every guard is a bare-chested Nair in a white mundu with a dark sash and topknot, holding a spear or matchlock. There are no helmets and no Europeans. Minor point: the plinth of one pillar near the right of the hall terrace (about x 0.81, y 0.41) has a tiny carved band. At 400% zoom its squiggles look faintly like glyphs; at print size it reads as ornament, so it is worth retouching only if desired. Ibrahim speaks from off panel, at the camera position on the road, so the tail points to the bottom edge. The open sky at upper left gives room for the balloon. v01 is rejected for a helmeted European-looking soldier and its photographic rendering.

v02 is acceptable and the edit worked. Ibrahim faces screen right and his visible right cheek is now unmarked. The gateway is built of rough red laterite blocks. The speaking Nair guard raises an open palm in three-quarter view with his mouth clear. Nagoji is in the foreground, bare-headed in his collarless cream shirt and dhoti, with bandaged hands, his head turned sharply toward the guards. The red flag carries a white conch. Notes: (1) Through the gate stands a whitewashed two-storey building with tiled roofs and a small tiled tower with finials. It reads as Kerala palace architecture (like Padmanabhapuram), not a church or fort. If the author finds it colonial-looking, paint it out to the open pillared hall. (2) Nagoji's sleeves are rolled up. (3) Note only: his ear ornament is a small hanging drop. Lettering can go on the plain laterite wall at upper right (the guard's balloon, near his head) and in the sky at top centre (the caption). v01 is rejected because Ibrahim's scar is on his visible right cheek and the gate is pale grey dressed stone.

v02 is acceptable and follows the correction. The background is the hall compound: the tiled hall on carved dark pillars at left, the laterite outer wall, palms and the still inlet with small country boats. There is no European fort, church or ship. Nagoji's bandaged hand still rests on the flaxen mane while the horse tosses its head away toward the groom. The groom is a bare-chested Kerala stable hand with a topknot and white mundu, so he cannot be mistaken for Ibrahim. Minor points: (1) The horse is a medium red chestnut, not dark liver-chestnut, but it matches the horse picked for panel 1.2. (2) Only two digits of Nagoji's bandaged hand show; the rest are buried in the mane, which is plausible. (3) Faint stubble shading on Nagoji's chin, within tolerance. (4) Note only: his ear ornament is a small hanging drop. There is wide clear sky across the top centre for the caption. v01 is rejected for a European fort and church on the headland, a European ship and a dockside crane.

v02 is acceptable. The edit fixed the far end and kept the rest. The shot is from behind at the top of the stone steps. Nagoji is bare-headed, with curly hair caught back, a long-sleeved cream shirt and dhoti, bandaged wrists, and a small gold stud and moustache tip in his partial profile. Ibrahim wears his white turban, teal short coat and striped shoulder cloth. The pillars are carved with vines and tigers, the rafters are dark and the floor has mats. Bare-chested, topknotted courtiers in white mundus sit either side of a clear lane, and the open side with the sea below is on screen left. At the far end, Varma sits cross-legged in the cream-and-gold turban with the peacock-feather crest, bare-chested, with the cloth over one shoulder and gold necklaces. His head is bowed over an unlettered map, so his eyes are hidden. Ramayyan, thin, balding and in white, sits at a low table on screen right. The red banner shows a silver conch with no lettering, the lamps are open-wick brass, and the incense wisp is gone. Minor points: Varma's face is only about 25 px wide, and a heavy jaw outline with chin shadow can suggest a faint beard line under magnification, but at reading size it reads as moustache and clean chin. The guards beside the banner have short beards and cross-straps, which is fine. The sky at upper left and the rafter band leave clean room for both captions. v01 remains unacceptable: the king is bare-headed with a topknot and bearded.

Acceptable. Varma matches the face sheet: cream-and-gold turban with the jewelled peacock-feather crest, bare-chested, cloth over one shoulder, gold necklaces, Vaishnavite forehead lines, spear against his shoulder, eyes down on the map. The map carries no writing. Ramayyan matches his sheet (thin, receding hair, plain white cloth, no sacred thread) and writes on unlettered palm leaves at the king's left hand (screen right). The open side is on screen left and the lamps are open-wick brass. Minor deviations: Ramayyan is lit and mid-sized rather than small and in shadow. The sword hilt is bright polished gold rather than worn smooth. Through the open side are a European-style fort with domed sentry turrets and square-rigged ships, which 2.1 does not show. The platform dressing (cushion, conch banner on the right wall) differs slightly from 2.5's throne seat. Panel 2.1 must be regenerated to match this king.

Round-3 fixes landed. (1) The white-bearded elder at the king's left hand (screen right) is gone. Ramayyan sits there instead: thin, balding crown, curly black hair at the sides, white cloth, writing with a stylus on stacked unlettered leaves. That reads as the man in 2.2 and 2.4. Two small leftovers you can see when zoomed in: he has a small moustache (the sheet and 2.2/2.4 show him clean-shaven), and his white cloth hangs over one shoulder, leaving part of his chest bare. At this background size his face is about 25 px, so neither reads at print scale. (2) Varma keeps the cream-and-gold turban with the jewelled peacock-feather crest, a bare chest and gold necklaces. His head is bowed over an unlettered map, eyes hidden. He sits cross-legged on a low wooden platform, and the stone steps from v02 are gone. (3) The fort beyond the open side at the far left is gone: only sea, palms and a green headland. (4) Ibrahim's scar is now a thinner, muted pinkish line on his own left cheek (the camera-facing side), from near the ear down through the beard to the jaw. It is no longer bright orange or red. Nothing else got worse: the foreground is the same as v02. Nagoji is in clean profile with a thick curled moustache, a clean chin, a cream collarless shirt and bandaged hands. His hair is loose rather than tied back, which the edit asked to keep. His ear ornament is a small gold ball drop rather than a stud (noted only, as the author has not decided). The open-side lamps are brass with open wicks, the conch banner on red has no lettering, and there is no text anywhere. The courtiers are bare-chested with topknots and white mundus. Lettering space: plain sky at upper left (x 0 to 0.4, y 0 to 0.18) and a plain grey band at upper right (x 0.5 to 0.92, y 0.09 to 0.17). Neither covers a face or the action. v02 is still unacceptable (white-bearded elder in Ramayyan's place, a fort on the headland, a stepped stone dais), so there is no backup.

Acceptable. Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin, sharp features, receding hair, upper body wrapped in plain white cloth, no jewellery, no sacred thread. He sits at a low table with palm-leaf bundles that carry no script, a black ink pot and a stylus, and he glances toward the newcomers. In the foreground, two bare-chested topknotted men in white mundus whisper with sound hands. Light comes from the open side on screen left. The sky at upper left takes the caption cleanly. Minor deviations: the background guards wear white turbans, and one wears a shirt with cross-belts, unlike the bare-chested topknotted guards in 2.5. The hall opens at ground level onto a busy quay with European ships and a fort wall. The floor is polished stone rather than the mats of 2.1. A thin painted frame line runs along the image edge and should be cropped in layout.

The edit worked. The v02 throne and stone dais are gone, and Varma now sits cross-legged on a small mat on a low wooden platform. He still has his cream-and-gold turban with the jewelled peacock-feather crest, his moustache, gold necklaces and the cream-and-gold shoulder cloth. Nagoji, Ibrahim, the seated rows, the guards, the lamps and the conch banner are unchanged from v02. The hall plan holds: the open side and the sea are on screen left, matching 2.1 to 2.4. Three small points, none a reason to reject: (1) Nagoji is medium-sized in frame, not as small against the hall as the script asks. (2) Ibrahim shows a tiny ear stud on his right ear, which his sheet does not have. It is barely visible at this size. (3) Varma has no spear against his shoulder here, and the script does not ask for one in 2.5. Nagoji and Ibrahim are seen from behind, so Nagoji's face, chin and ear stud cannot be checked. His loose curly hair, cream shirt, dhoti and bandaged hands match the chapter 6 row. There is no text, no gore and no anachronism. The caption can sit in the sky at top left (about x 0.01 to 0.22, y 0.03 to 0.30) or across the rafters at top right (about x 0.40 to 0.95, y 0.0 to 0.15).

v02 does what the edit asked for. Varma's eyes are down on the map and one hand rests flat on it. The guards wear white head cloths and Ibrahim gestures in profile on screen left of Nagoji. v01 stays rejected: Varma has his chin on his hand and looks toward the camera, and one guard wears a red turban. Minor notes on v02: (1) A distant hill fort shows through the open side. It reads as Indian, not European, and matches neighbouring panel 3.3. (2) There are faint specks along the map's lower edge, too small to read as writing. (3) Nagoji is seen from behind, so his moustache, chin and ear ornament cannot be checked. His bow is a shallow dip of head and shoulders, which fits the script. (4) Lettering fits on the plain sunlit wall above Nagoji's head (x 0.26 to 0.52, y 0 to 0.2) and between the banners above Varma.

Clean. Varma's eyes and brow match the sheet (thick brows, Vaishnavite namam, dark curls at the temples), and a cream turban with gold bands and a jewel shows at the top edge. The eyes look hard to the side: steady, not soft. Both eyes sit inside the middle half of the width, and the temples fade into plain dark shadow at each end, leaving room for the two captions (left x 0 to 0.18 and right x 0.77 to 1.0). The frame has white letterbox bands above and below the art strip (rows 0 to 98 and 570 to 723). The layout tool trims these automatically, so they are not painted boxes.

The edit is clean. Varma sits cross-legged on a mat on a low wooden platform, with no throne or chair left. His face matches the sheet, and he wears the cream-and-gold turban with the peacock crest, a bare chest, gold necklaces and the cream-and-gold shoulder cloth. Ramayyan matches his sheet and holds a stylus and palm-leaf bundle. Nagoji is seen from behind with the gold ear stud and the moustache tip showing, and his chin is not visible. Two small notes: Nagoji's hair hangs loose in a low bunch rather than clearly tied back (the bible allows loose or tied back), and Ramayyan sits on the king's mat rather than at the low table seen in 3.4. Neither is a blocker. There is no text, and the open side of the hall is on screen left as scripted. The plain grey wall above both seated figures and the sky at the upper left give clear lettering space.

The edit is clean. Varma sits cross-legged on a mat on a low wooden platform, with no throne left. His profile matches the sheet, and he wears the cream-and-gold turban with the jewelled peacock crest, a bare chest and cream-and-gold cloth. Ramayyan, in plain white cloth with no jewellery, sits at a low table at the platform's front corner. Nagoji stands on the floor in a cream shirt and dhoti with bandaged hands, bare-headed and unarmed. He has a thick moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a small gold stud. The figures run left to right as the script asks, with the closed wall behind them. There is no text, and the hands are sound. The large plain wall between Ramayyan and Nagoji leaves ample room for the four staggered balloons. A guard is cropped at the left edge, which is harmless.

v02 fixes the setting. It now shows the coastal hall from panel 3.4: dark carved pillar, palms and sea through the open side, a brass lamp with open wicks, the grey wall with its frieze band, the platform step, a polished floor and a mat. Nagoji wears a plain long-sleeved cream shirt over a white dhoti with no sash. The sleeves cover his wrists and the linen wrappings are clean. Varma's bare forearm, gold bangle and gold-bordered cream cloth enter from the left, and only his index and middle fingers are extended (thumb on top, ring and little fingers curled). v01 stays rejected: it is set in a prison cell with a barred window, a wall ring and chain, and gives Nagoji a red sash. Minor notes on v02: (1) Nagoji's wrapped hands hang loosely together in front of his body rather than strictly at his sides, but they are still and at the far edge of frame as the script asks. (2) Varma's two fingers are spread slightly, but they clearly point down at Nagoji's hands. (3) No faces are in frame. Both speakers are off-panel above: Ramayyan's tail goes to the top edge at centre, Nagoji's to the top edge above his body. (4) Clear plain wall for both lines at x 0.33 to 0.78, y 0.02 to 0.33.

Clean. Varma matches the V13 sheet (cream-and-gold turban with the jewelled peacock-feather crest, pearl earrings, curled moustache, gold necklaces, bare chest, gold-bordered cloth over one shoulder). He faces the camera with his eyes already sliding away, and the open arch to sky and palms is on screen left as scripted. The brass standing lamp has open wicks and there is no text. The plain wall on the right half is clear for the caption. The figure has a faint cut-out outline against the background, which is cosmetic only.

v02 follows the edit instruction. The dais, the carved chairs and the turbaned seated figures are gone. Behind Ramayyan there is only the closed wall, the conch-on-red banner and plain floor. The one courtier at far left is bare-chested in a white mundu with a topknot. Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin, receding curly hair, plain white cloth, no jewellery, no sacred thread, profile toward the mat, pointing with the stylus, palm-leaf bundle at his hip. Nagoji has a thick curled moustache and clean chin. He is bare-headed, with hair half tied back, and wears a collarless cream shirt and dhoti with bandaged hands. He crouches stiffly onto the woven mat. The brass lamp has open wicks. There is no text. The sky at upper centre-right is clear for both of Ramayyan's balloons. Minor points: (1) The two guards wear white short-sleeved tunics with crossed belts, but the guards in 5.1 and 5.2 are bare-chested. The r1 correction kept these guards. (2) Through the open side we see palms and a distant hill fort, not the sea of 4.5 and 5.x. The fort reads as Indian, not European. (3) Nagoji's ear ornament is a small gold drop, not a flush stud. This is noted only, since the author has not yet decided which is canonical. v01 is still unacceptable: dais, turbaned courtiers in stitched shirts.

Round-3 fix landed. The rust-red sash is gone completely, and the collarless long-sleeved cream shirt now hangs straight over a plain cream dhoti with no coloured cloth at the waist. That matches panels 4.2 and 4.4 (v02 frames), which use the same shirt, dhoti, brass open-wick lamp and woven mat. Nothing else got worse. Nagoji matches the sheet: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin with only light stubble, long curly black hair (worn loose, which the bible allows), bare-headed and lean. The script beat holds: he sits cross-legged on the mat, talking, with one bandaged hand flat in the air shaping a low wall and the other bandaged hand resting on his knee. Both hands are anatomically sound. The open side of the hall is on screen right, with a laterite wall, a carved timber pillar, a tiled eave and the Kerala coast. The bastion stain at upper left has soft, borderless smoky edges. It shows a thick, low Portuguese bastion with gunners in buff coats and morions, and a cannonball skipping off the slope in stone dust. There is no flag, no text, no blood and no glass lantern. Note only: the ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop rather than a stud (the author has not decided). Clear sky in the upper centre (about x 0.35 to 0.67, y 0.02 to 0.33) has room for the caption at the top and Nagoji's balloon below it, above the raised hand. v02 is still unacceptable because of the sash.

v02 honours the correction. The padre's cassock is black to the throat, with a plain black standing collar and no white tab or edge. The stain holds only the stocky, dark-bearded padre with the cross held high and the column of musketeers. The musketeers wear broad tilted plumed hats and buff leather coats and carry matchlocks, with no red or blue, no flags and no buildings, against plain sepia haze. The haze is soft and borderless. Nagoji sits cross-legged on the woven mat at lower left, in normal colour, talking. He has a curled moustache and clean chin, is bare-headed with loose curly hair, and wears a collarless cream shirt and dhoti with bandaged hands. Only a thin brown waist cord shows, no red sash. Varma's hand with the gold bead bracelet grips the dark spear shaft at the right foreground edge, with his head out of frame. The brass lamp has an open wick. There is no text. The pale haze at the upper right and upper centre is clear for both of Nagoji's balloons. Minor points: (1) The hall's open side and sea show at screen left, behind the pillar. Neighbours 4.2 and 4.3 put the open side on screen right. The stain dominates, so this barely reads. (2) Varma's forearm and a sliver of his gold-bordered cloth are in frame, not only the hand. He grips rather than taps. The r1 correction kept both. (3) Nagoji is medium-small rather than tiny. (4) The ear ornament is a small gold drop, noted only. v01 is still unacceptable: white collar edge on the cassock, and a church and town in the stain.

Acceptable. Varma matches the sheet: cream-and-gold turban with the jewelled peacock-feather crest, pearl earrings, curled moustache, bare chest, gold necklaces and gold-bordered cloth. He leans over the unrolled map with one finger on a river mouth where it meets the sea. The map carries no writing, place names or numerals. The top-left inset is cleanly bordered and shows Ramayyan's hand and stylus on a palm-leaf bundle against plain white cloth, with sound hand anatomy. The leaf carries only faint, blurred scratch marks with no legible letters, the level the prompt audit allowed. The brass lamp has an open wick, the banner is a conch on red, and the guard is bare-chested. The plain wall between the inset and Varma, and the sky at right, give room for all three lettering lines. Tail notes: Nagoji (copy 0) is off-panel behind the camera, so his tail ends on the left frame edge just below the inset. Ramayyan (copy 2) is seen only as the hand in the inset, so his tail ends at the inset's upper right edge, where his body is. | r5: v02 edit (batch 45): hall background swapped so the open sea side is on screen left; Varma and inset unchanged. Geometry carried from v01 (composition unchanged).

v02 fixes the round-1 fault and is acceptable. The hall is in bright daylight with carved dark pillars, a polished floor and a brass standing lamp with open wicks. The open side on screen right shows a sunlit sea and palms under a blue sky, with no storeroom clutter. One background guard stands at the left, bare-chested in a white mundu with a red sash, crossed leather belts, a topknot and a spear. The night stain bleeds softly into the hall behind Nagoji with no frame. It shows the view between a black horse's ears down a moonlit quay, with sails on the water and a burning warehouse. There are no flags, crosses, signboards or lettering in it. Nagoji matches the sheet: eyes closed, thick curled moustache, clean chin, bandaged hands, collarless cream shirt and dhoti, bare-headed with his hair loose. Minor notes: (1) His ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop rather than a flush stud (noted only, as the author has not decided). (2) He wears a twisted rust-red cloth at the waist. The 5.1 prompt does not forbid it and 4.3 v02 shows the same thing, but 5.2 and 5.4 have no sash, so a later touch-up could remove it for consistency on the page. The caption fits in the upper-right sky or in the dark night sky at the top of the stain. v01 is still unacceptable: the real hall is at night and full of storeroom clutter.

v02 is acceptable. It shows the Travancore coastal hall: dark carved timber pillars, a tiled roof edge, a polished floor, a brass open-wick lamp, and a sunlit sea and palms through the open side on screen right. Two Nair guards stand in the background, bare-chested in white mundus with red sashes, crossed leather belts and topknots, holding spears. This matches the guard in 5.1. There are no European figures, rings or chairs. The only foreground element is a soft, out-of-focus bare brown shoulder with a cream-and-gold cloth at the lower left, with no face and no beard. It is larger than a sliver but reads clearly as the king. Nagoji is on model: eyes open toward the king, thick curled moustache, clean chin, collarless cream shirt and dhoti, bandaged hands. His hands and anatomy are sound. There is clear sky above his head and a wide clear sky at upper right for both balloons. Note only: his ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop, not a flush stud. v01 is still unacceptable (a Portuguese court with morion-helmeted soldiers and a ruffed grandee).

Clean. Varma matches the sheet: cream-and-gold turban with the jewelled peacock crest, bare chest, gold necklaces, Vaishnavite mark, head lifted from the map, eyes narrowed, mouth open. Ramayyan is at screen right: thin, receding curly hair, plain white cloth, lips closed, stylus paused on the palm-leaf bundle. The open side of the hall is on screen left. The flag is an unlettered silver conch on red, the guards wear white with crossed belts, the lamp is brass with open wicks, and the map carries no text. Two minor points: Varma's finger rests on the hills rather than the river mouth from 4.5, and the background guards differ in dress from those in 5.5. Open sky between the turban and Ramayyan holds the balloon.

All three round-3 fixes landed and nothing else got worse. (1) The heavyset seated man with gold necklaces and his wooden chair are gone. The carved pillar base and the polished floor are painted cleanly in their place, with no leftover traces and no other seated courtier or official. (2) Both background guards are now bare-chested Nair guards with black topknots, white mundus, dark red waist sashes and crossed leather belts, each holding a spear upright. They match 5.1 and 5.2, with no turbans or tunics. (3) The walled hilltop fort is replaced by a plain green, palm-covered headland, with no walls or towers. Everything that was right in v02 is kept. Nagoji is on model: seated cross-legged on his woven mat, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, long curly hair, collarless cream shirt and dhoti, bare-headed, no sash or sword. His bandaged hands are sound: the right hand is open in a level gesture toward the king and the left rests on his knee. The out-of-focus bare shoulder with cream-and-gold cloth and gold armlet at the left reads as the king, and the open side with the sea is on screen right. The brass standing lamp has open wicks, and there is no text, pseudo-text, blood or anachronism. Notes only: (a) Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop rather than a flush stud (author undecided). (b) The king's ear ornament, barely visible at the extreme top-left corner, is a large gold ball rather than the pearl drop on his sheet. It is out of focus and could sit under a balloon. (c) As in v02, the hall pillars are carved stone with an elephant relief, while 5.2 was described as having timber pillars. This is minor. Lettering: Ramayyan's off-panel line can go at the upper left over the blurred pillar and wall, with its tail to the left frame edge (he stands at the king's left hand, off screen left). Nagoji's two lines fit in the clear sky between the pillars above his head, about x 0.46 to 0.68 and y 0.02 to 0.17, and in the upper-right sky, about x 0.76 to 0.92 and y 0.02 to 0.16. Neither area covers a face or a hand. v02 stays unacceptable: it has the extra seated man, turbaned and tunic-clad guards, and the hilltop fort.

The edit worked. The throne and red bolster are gone, and Varma now sits cross-legged on a woven mat on a low carved wooden platform. His face, turban, crest, jewellery and both hands are unchanged from v01 and match varma-v1. Ramayyan's face and his writing pose are unchanged and match his sheet. No text was added. The beat reads: Varma has a faint sideways smirk with his head not turned, and Ramayyan writes without looking up. The open side is on screen left. Clear sky between the pillars (top centre to top right) and at top left leaves room for both short balloons. Minor points: (1) Ramayyan's table is a taller standing table whose leg drops in front of the platform edge, and no legs or cloth of his show beneath it, so his lower body is a little ambiguous. (2) No map lies before Varma, unlike in 5.3. Neither is a reason to reject.

Edit is clean. The throne is gone: Varma sits cross-legged on a mat on the low wooden platform, with the same face, crested cream-and-gold turban and the spear upright beside him. Ramayyan sits at his left hand (screen right), Nagoji is on his mat with his back to us (gold stud just visible), the open side and the sea are on screen left, and there is no text. The white wall above the platform and the sky at top left are free for the Varma balloon and the caption.

Edit is clean. Varma now sits cross-legged on a mat on a low wooden block on the platform instead of the lion-armed throne; his face, turban, spear and pose are kept. Ramayyan is unchanged: near right, stylus held still above the leaf bundle, hands sound. The open side is on screen left and there is no text. Ramayyan's two balloons can go on the plain wall above his head or in the sky at upper left.

v02 (the correction) is clean and follows the script and the chapter 6 bible row. The setting is the Travancore coastal hall: dark carved pillars, laterite wall, tiled rafters, and the open sea side on screen right. Bare-chested courtiers in white mundu with topknots sit behind him, Nair spear guards wear dark sashes, and the brass lamps have open wicks. The foreground is only the dark carved platform edge and a gold-bordered cream hem. Nagoji is bare-headed in a collarless cream shirt and dhoti, with his jaw set and his eyes level on the platform. His clean bandaged hands grip the cloth on his knees, sleeves down to the bandages, and the hand anatomy is sound. Upper left and upper centre are plain wall, with room for all three lettering areas. Minor notes, none a reason to reject: (1) The ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop, not a stud. This matches the sheet, and the author has not yet decided which is canonical. (2) There is faint light stubble on the chin, within the bible's 'light stubble at most'. (3) His hair is loose, not tied back as the correction asked. The bible allows loose, and it matches 6.1. (4) A tiny, hazy fortified headland sits on the far horizon at right. It is too small to read as European and matches the distant headland already seen in 6.1. v01 is not acceptable: it is a Portuguese/Goa setting with helmeted, breastplated European soldiers, a seated official in an embroidered coat, an iron wall ring and a European desk.

Edit is clean. The carved throne is gone: Varma sits cross-legged on a mat and red cushion on the low wooden platform, gesturing, with the same face and turban.
